description:
ComputeCluster resource for running long-running container workloads.

A ComputeCluster provides the setup-owned machine boundary for containers.
Alien may manage the worker fleet inside that boundary when setup grants
`compute-cluster/management`.

## Architecture

- **Setup** creates cloud resources: ASGs/MIGs/VMSSs, IAM roles, security groups
- **Alien** manages allowed fleet operations: machine count, runtime
  machine image rollout and, on AWS, the machine type within one CPU architecture
- A node agent runs on each machine from the selected runtime image channel

## Example

```rust
use alien_core::{CapacityGroup, ComputeCluster, MachineProfile};

let cluster = ComputeCluster::new("compute".to_string())
    .capacity_group(CapacityGroup {
        group_id: "general".to_string(),
        instance_type: None,
        profile: Some(MachineProfile {
            cpu: "4.0".to_string(),
            memory_bytes: 16 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
            ephemeral_storage_bytes: 20 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
            architecture: None,
            gpu: None,
        }),
        min_size: 1,
        max_size: 5,
        scale_policy: None,
        nested_virtualization: None,
    })
    .build();
```

items.description:
Capacity group definition.

A capacity group represents machines with identical hardware profiles.
Each group becomes a separate Auto Scaling Group (AWS), Managed Instance Group (GCP),
or VM Scale Set (Azure).

groupId.description: Unique identifier for this capacity group (must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens)

instanceType.description:
Provider machine selected at deployment time.
`alien.ts` should declare portable requirements; preflight materialization
fills this field from `StackSettings.compute`.

minSize.description: Minimum number of machines (can be 0 for scale-to-zero)

nestedVirtualization.description:
Require instance types that expose nested virtualization (VT-x/EPT)
to guest VMs. This is needed by workloads that boot nested VMs inside
containers.
When true, the controller's instance-type selector is constrained
to a vetted nested-virt-capable allowlist.

oneOf.description: Machine resource profile (auto-derived from instance_type if not specified)
CPU architecture required or provided by this machine profile.

cpu.description:
CPU cores per machine (hardware total) - stored as string to preserve precision
(e.g., "8.0", "4.5")

oneOf.description:
Source-declared scale policy and installer-editable bounds.

Older stacks only have `minSize` and `maxSize`; planners derive an exact
fixed/autoscale policy from those selected bounds when this field is absent.
A fixed-size pool where the installer can choose the fixed machine count.

default.description: Default value recommended when no installer override is supplied.

oneOf.description: An autoscaling pool with separately bounded min and max counts.

default.description: Default value recommended when no installer override is supplied.
Default value recommended when no installer override is supplied.

capacityGroups.description:
Capacity groups defining the machine pools for this cluster.
Each group becomes a separate ASG/MIG/VMSS.

containerCidr.description:
Container CIDR block for internal container networking.
Auto-generated as "10.244.0.0/16" if not specified.
Each machine gets a /24 subnet from this range.

dynamicContainerPool.description:
Pool reserved for containers created after a deployment is installed.
If absent, the runtime uses the `general` pool when it exists.

failureDomainSpread.description:
Requested failure-domain spread keyed by capacity group.
Empty preserves the existing aggregate layout.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the container cluster.
Must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores.

oneOf.description:
Explicit grants for the node identity, keyed by concrete resource ID.
Independent of workload permission profiles; absent grants no data access.
Reference to a built-in permission set by name (e.g., "storage/data-read")

description.description: Human-readable description of what this permission set allows

id.description: Unique identifier for the permission set (e.g., "storage/data-read")

binding.description: How to bind the permissions (stack vs resource scope)

notResources.description:
ARN patterns rendered as IAM `NotResource`, in place of `resources`. Its one use is a
tag-on-create grant whose implied check AWS authorizes against no resource; the build
refuses it anywhere else.
